sections.title: The Vision of Joshua the High Priest
observations: In this vision, Zechariah sees Joshua, the high priest, standing before the angel of the Lord, with Satan standing at his right side to accuse him. This scene illustrates the spiritual reality of the ongoing conflict between God's people and their adversary, Satan.

Joshua represents the people of Israel, who have returned from exile and are in need of restoration. His filthy garments symbolize the sin and guilt of the nation, while the presence of Satan as the accuser highlights the need for divine intervention.

sections.title: The Cleansing of Joshua
observations: The angel of the Lord rebukes Satan, declaring that the Lord has chosen Jerusalem and that Joshua's sins are removed. This act of cleansing signifies God's grace and mercy towards His people, emphasizing that their restoration is not based on their merit but on God's sovereign choice.

The exchange between the angel and Satan demonstrates God's authority over accusations and His commitment to redeem His people. The clean garments placed on Joshua symbolize the righteousness that God provides.

importantVerses.commentary: The Lord rebukes Satan, showing His authority over the accuser and affirming His choice of Jerusalem.
Joshua's filthy garments are removed, symbolizing the removal of sin and guilt, and he is clothed with pure garments.

questions: What does the vision of Joshua teach us about the nature of spiritual warfare?
How does the cleansing of Joshua relate to the concept of justification in the New Testament?
In what ways can we apply the themes of accusation and divine grace in our own lives?
